title: Why? #3 remade: double a 2×2 matrix, its determinant? (predict-first, Remotion, drive, 22 s)

captions.instagram:
NDA Maths · Matrices & Determinants
Double every number in a 2×2 matrix. Its determinant becomes… A ×2 · B ×4 · C same
Comment your guess before you watch 👇

Why? #3. The rows of a 2×2 matrix are two arrows, and |det| is the area between them. A = [3 1; 1 2] → |A| = 3·2 − 1·1 = 5.
Double row 1: area 10 (2 copies). Double row 2 too (that's 2A): area 20 (4 copies) → |2A| = 4|A| → B, not 2|A|.
Scale by any k: area × k². For an n×n matrix: |kA| = kⁿ|A|.

NDA 2025 (II) asked exactly this (Maths Q44): Statement I: det(mX) = mⁿ det(X). Statement II: multiplying one row by m multiplies det by m. Answer (a): both true, and II explains I.
